1.support: This study assesses the effects of three PEEP titration strategies on MP, hemodynamic parameters, and oxygen delivery in twenty ARDS patients with V–V ECMO.

2.support: We enrolled 20 patients with severe ARDS according to the Berlin definition [23] during the first three days of V–V ECMO treatment

3.support: We enrolled 20 patients with severe ARDS according to the Berlin definition [23] during the first three days of V–V ECMO treatment in the intensive care unit

4.support: I looked for a statement that all consecutive eligible patients were screened and enrolled and did not find one; the report states only that 20 patients were enrolled.

5.support: Details for the sample size calculation are given in the Supplement.

6.support: PEEP was initially set to 10 cm H2O representing the lowest ELSO recommendation (PEEPELSO) [19] and respiratory mechanics as well as hemodynamics were measured. A dynamic recruitment maneuver to standardize the history of lung volume [27] was performed followed by a decremental PEEP trial

7.support: Correct positioning was verified by a ratio of change in esophageal pressure to the change in airway pressure of 0.8–1.2 as previously described [25].

8.support: I looked for any description of blinding of the investigators assessing the respiratory mechanics and hemodynamic outcomes and found none; the same operators applied the PEEP strategies and recorded the outcomes, and no blinding was possible for physiological measurements.

9.support: Twenty patients with severe ARDS treated with V–V ECMO were included in the analysis.

10.support: clinical variables were analyzed using repeated measures one-way ANOVA followed by Holm-Sidak's post-hoc test or Friedman's test for non-normally distributed data

11.support: Respiratory mechanics and hemodynamics were recorded once at each PEEP titration step after a 30-min equilibration period; I looked for repeated pre- and post-intervention measurements (interrupted time-series design) and found none.

12.support: The intervention (PEEP titration) was applied at the individual patient level, not at a group level.

nih.rationale: The rating is driven down from Good mainly by items 5 and 8 and the design's inherent limitations: the sample size of 20 was not justified by a sample-size calculation in the report (item 5, No), outcome assessors were not blinded (item 8, No), the sequence of PEEP strategies was not randomized as the authors acknowledge ('the sequence of different PEEP titration strategies was not randomized', Limitations), and measurements were single assessments per strategy rather than repeated time-series measurements (item 11, No). The study retains adequate quality: the question is clear (item 1), eligibility criteria are prespecified (item 2), patients are representative of the target population (item 3), the intervention is described in detail and applied consistently with standardized recruitment maneuvers and equilibration periods (item 6), outcomes are objective and measured with validated methods (item 7), there was no loss to follow-up (item 9), and appropriate repeated-measures statistics with p values were used (item 10). No single fatal flaw is present, so the study is rated Fair rather than Poor.
